review_notes: I read the whole target file and the neighbouring Counting files that define or reuse the same pieces: HistogramOverlapEnergy, HistogramBoxEnergy, GeometricWindowKernel, HistogramWindowOverlap and ProjectedHistogramError. I did not find a Mathlib lemma that gives a shorter proof of the weighted double-counting lemma, so I did not propose one. The final calc and the positivity side goals looked reasonable as written. I could not compile anything. The `gcongr` replacement in the second finding copies a pattern that compiles in GeometricWindowKernel, but the goal there is not identical to this one, so it is untested here.

findings.excerpt:
have hmesh : (B : ℝ)*channelMesh (channelFineCount m B) ≤ 1 := by
    refine (channelMesh_scale_bound hm hBpos).trans ?_
    simpa using Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le
findings.problem: This four-line proof of `B * channelMesh ≤ 1` is repeated almost verbatim in about nine places. Examples are HistogramBoxEnergy (`geometric_histogram_window_length`), HistogramOverlapEnergy, GeometricWindowKernel (twice), HistogramWindowBounds (twice), CoarseCoefficientVariation, LogMassBilinear and GeometricFeatureBounds. In the target it is also never named in a later step. `by linarith` in `hK` picks it up implicitly from context, so a reader has to work out why the block is there.
findings.proposed_change: Prove `channelMesh_mul_le_one (hm : 0 < m) (hB : 1 ≤ B) : (B : ℝ) * channelMesh (channelFineCount m B) ≤ 1` once, next to `channelMesh_scale_bound`. Its proof is the existing three-line `refine ... .trans ?_; simpa using Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le ...`. Here, replace the block with `have hmesh := channelMesh_mul_le_one hm hB`. Keep the lemma's statement explicit so the reader sees what `hK`'s `linarith` or `gcongr` uses. All the other copies can shrink the same way. I did not find an existing lemma with this statement, so it would be new.
findings.benefit: This removes about four lines per use site and gives the fact one searchable name. The main argument is shorter and the dependence of `hK` on the mesh bound is explicit.

findings.excerpt:
refine (histogramWindow_overlap hB0 ht hLU (channelFineCount_pos hm hBpos) S i).trans ?_
    exact add_le_add (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by linarith) ht.le) le_rfl
findings.problem: The overlap bound `(B*mesh+U-L)/t+1` is weakened to `(1+U-L)/t+1` by manually assembling `add_le_add`, `div_le_div_of_nonneg_right` and a `linarith` that silently reads `hmesh`. This is a monotonicity step, and `gcongr` expresses it directly.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the two lines with a single term: `have hK : ∀ i, ... := fun i => (histogramWindow_overlap hB0 ht hLU (channelFineCount_pos hm hBpos) S i).trans (by gcongr)`. This is the form used for the same step in `geometricWindowKernel_bounds`, where `hmesh` is also in context. Keep `hmesh` visible, as in the first finding.
findings.benefit: The proof states the idea (the mesh term is at most 1 and division by t is monotone) without naming lemma arguments. It also matches how the sibling file handles the identical inequality.

findings.excerpt: theorem sum_selected_cells_le_overlap {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
findings.problem: This theorem and its whole proof are a character-for-character copy of the private `local_mass_sum` in HistogramOverlapEnergy.lean. Both have the same statement, and both proofs use `he`, `simp_rw [he]`, `sum_comm`, `mul_sum` and `hc`. Because `local_mass_sum` is private, the same 15-line proof is maintained twice.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the proof here and reuse the existing one. Either make `local_mass_sum` non-private, or move this theorem into HistogramOverlapEnergy (which this file already imports transitively through HistogramBoxEnergy) and drop the private copy. The call at line 65, `sum_selected_cells_le_overlap S J w hw _ hK`, then needs no change.
findings.benefit: This cuts about 16 duplicated lines. Any later improvement to the double-counting argument is made once.
